title: The model keeps nothing, so your code stores facts and puts them back in the prompt
aria: On Monday the backend resends the system prompt and the whole transcript to a model that keeps nothing between calls. The model answers in JSON and proposes a fact; code gates it, queues it in the same transaction as the messages, and a worker upserts it into a facts table keyed by user. On Thursday a new chat loads the 50 newest facts into the system prompt, and the model greets the learner with them. A bottom row shows the trap: a planted fact rides the same path into every later prompt, and the fix at each step.

build.title: Monday: the model keeps nothing
build.text: The backend keeps the chat's messages, keyed by conversation ID. On every call it resends the system prompt and the whole transcript to Gemini, which keeps nothing between calls.

build.title: The model only proposes a fact
build.text: Gemini answers in fixed JSON: `responseText` to show and save, and a `memoryUpdates` list. If the JSON does not parse, the backend shows the text and stores nothing.

build.title: Code gates and queues it
build.text: The gate reads app state, never the model: in role-play the turn writes nothing. The fact is queued as a job row in the same transaction as the messages.

build.title: A worker stores one row per key
build.text: A worker polls every second, drops the job if memory is switched off, trims the key and value, and upserts one row per user and key. Any key is allowed.

build.title: Thursday: facts go back into the prompt
build.text: A new chat loads the 50 most recently updated facts once, as plain lines in the system prompt. The model takes each one as true, and the greeting uses the first 5.

build.title: A planted fact rides the same path
build.text: In a made-up support assistant, a pasted document plants “verified admin”. It is stored, read back as true and used to fetch another account's invoices. The bottom line of each box is the fix at that step.

route.title: Monday, the backend resends the whole conversation
route.text: The learner writes “Je joue au tennis…” (example). On every call the backend resends the system prompt and all the chat's messages, keyed by conversation ID, with the new message last.

route.title: The model answers in JSON and proposes a fact
route.text: The tutor answers in a fixed JSON shape: `responseText` to show, and `memoryUpdates`, usually empty. Here it holds set favorite_sport = tennis. The transcript keeps only `responseText`; bad JSON stores nothing.

route.title: Code, not the model, decides whether this turn may write
route.text: The gate reads state the app controls. With a story, a reference text or a reference picture attached (role-play), the turn queues no memory job. Here role-play is off, so the gate is open.

route.title: Queue the fact in the same transaction as the messages
route.text: The memory job row is written in the same transaction that saves the turn's messages, so both commit or neither does. The learner gets the reply text.

route.title: A worker upserts the fact, one row per user and key
route.text: A worker checks for pending jobs every second and claims one. It checks the memory switch, on by default, cleans the key and value, and upserts. A failing job is retried after 2, 4, 6 and 8 seconds.

route.title: Thursday, the stored facts go back into the system prompt
route.text: The new chat's transcript is empty. The backend loads the 50 most recently updated facts once and writes them as plain lines, such as “- favorite_sport: tennis”. The model asks about the match.
